findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen AC3's proving command to include an automated string assertion for the key semantic phrases (e.g. add `'exactly once' in sec` and `'not injected into round_b'` or equivalent to the marker check), rather than relying solely on manual comparison, so the accuracy claim produces auditable evidence.
evidence: 'verified by manual comparison with `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` plus the marker command above'
AC2 marker list does not include 'exactly once' or 'not injected' as checked strings
AC3 accuracy claim is completion-relevant but has no reproducible automated evidence
findings.finding: AC3's proving method for the semantic accuracy claim ('matching `CodeReviewBatchRunner`') is stated as 'manual comparison', which does not produce reproducible, auditable evidence that the subsection text correctly captures the source behavior (e.g. 'exactly once in round_a' and 'not injected into round_b'). The automated marker check in AC2 only confirms the strings 'round_a' and 'round_b' appear somewhere in the section, not that the prose accurately says 'exactly once' or 'not injected into round_b'.
scenarios: An executor writes prose that mentions round_a and round_b but misstates the injection semantics (e.g. says 'may be injected into round_a' rather than 'exactly once'); AC2 passes, AC3 manual comparison is subjective and leaves no audit trail.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the AC2 marker list (or add a dedicated AC3 command) to assert the presence of phrases like `'exactly once'` and `'not injected into round_b'` within the Round A/B subsection, e.g.: `sub=sec.split('#### Round A/B fan-in',1)[1].split('####',1)[0]; assert 'exactly once' in sub and 'not injected into round_b' in sub`

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or Approach step) that audits existing `docs/llm-framework.md` content for any pre-existing description of the four-pass gate, fan-in, or Pass-3 routing, and either removes/updates it or explicitly cross-references the new normative section to prevent internal contradiction.
evidence: AC verification commands use `split('Code-review project criteria',1)[1][:5000]` — they only inspect the NEW section, never checking pre-existing content for contradictions.
ABSENCE: no AC or approach step mentions auditing or updating existing `docs/llm-framework.md` prose that may already reference the four-pass gate behavior.
findings.finding: The acceptance criteria verify only that new headings and markers are ADDED to `docs/llm-framework.md`, but do not check whether existing content in the same document already partially or incorrectly describes the four-pass gate flows (fan-in, Pass-3 routing, eval resolution) in ways that the new section may contradict or render stale — creating internal inconsistency within the authoritative doc.
scenarios: Existing doc already has an informal or partial description of round_a/round_b fan-in that conflicts with the new normative section; a reader sees two contradictory accounts in the same file.
A later contributor treats the older passage as canonical (it appears earlier in the file) and the new normative section as supplemental, leading to misimplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step under Approach: 'Search `docs/llm-framework.md` for existing prose mentioning `round_a`, `round_b`, `Pass 3`, or `fan-in`; update or remove any partial descriptions that would conflict with the new normative section, or add a forward-reference to it.' Add a corresponding AC: 'No other passage in `docs/llm-framework.md` contradicts the new section's stated contract for Round A/B fan-in or Pass-3 routing.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that `#### Configuration error` documents behavior that is explicitly within the parent epic's (119f) contracted seam scope, or remove/relocate it; if the behavior was established by one of the six seam children, add a citation in the leaf plan tying it to that child's scope.
evidence: Parent epic (119f) seam decomposition lists six children covering: ids.py resolver, batch_runner.py fan-in, workflow_ops.py Pass-3 routing, eval_solver.py/eval.py eval admission, _llm_eval_commands.py CLI admission, docs/llm-framework.md contract — no 'configuration error' child.

Parent epic root-cause drop points (five named): criterion_prompt_id hardcodes plan-review prefix; CodeReviewBatchRunner iterates only built-ins; workflow_ops.py uses packaged routing map; eval_solver.py/eval.py exclude project ids; _llm_eval_commands.py admits only plan-review ids. None describes a missing-prompt/eval-spec configuration error.
Parent AC for docs child: 'The runtime contract is documented in docs/llm-framework.md (child 19dd).' — no mention of configuration error behavior being part of that contract.
Leaf AC2 requires the marker `configuration error` to appear in the documented section body, encoding this out-of-parent-scope behavior as a required contract element.
findings.finding: The leaf's `#### Configuration error` subheading documents a runtime contract aspect — 'an activated project criterion with a missing or invalid prompt/eval specification raises a located configuration error rather than silently falling back' — that has no corresponding entry in the parent epic's seam decomposition, root-cause drop-point list, or acceptance criteria. The parent enumerates exactly five drop points and six seam children; none is a 'configuration error on missing prompt/eval spec' guard. The leaf is thus documenting a contract behavior the parent's plan does not contain.
findings.location: Approach, item 4 (`#### Configuration error`) and Acceptance Criteria AC1/AC2 (marker `configuration error`)
scenarios: A future reader treats the `#### Configuration error` subsection as authoritative, but the behavior it documents may not have been implemented or may have been implemented differently by one of the seam children, since no seam child was scoped to 'raise a located configuration error for missing prompt/eval spec.'

The parent's plan-review attestation was signed against a scope that does not include this contract point; a downstream audit of 119f's coverage will find a discrepancy between parent-declared scope and what child 19dd actually documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Trace `#### Configuration error` to the specific seam child that implements the located-error behavior (likely fc72 or 8153), add a `[rebar:<child-id>]` citation in the leaf's Approach item 4, and verify that the parent's seam-child listing either already covers this point or update the parent to add it before re-reviewing the leaf.

findings.finding: Aspect 1 ('Round A/B fan-in') states that 'activated project criteria are fanned into the finder passes (round_a/round_b)' — but the code-review gate's round_a and round_b batch steps are closed, static lists of named overlay prompts (code-review-security, code-review-performance, etc.) with no dynamic injection point for project.<name> criteria. Project criteria enter the gate through effective_criteria()/effective_routing() for Pass-3 threshold resolution, not as finder passes in round_a/round_b. If no upstream seam child adds a structural injection mechanism into those batch steps, the documented 'fan-in to round_a/round_b' contract would misdescribe how project criteria actually flow through the pipeline.
findings.location: Approach section, Aspect 1: '#### Round A/B fan-in'

findings.finding: The AC2 marker list omits 'round_b' and 'project.' (or 'project.<name>'), both of which the Approach treats as normative content for the first subheading — meaning an implementation that correctly documents only round_a fan-in (the actual code behavior) or describes the logical criterion id without its 'project.<name>' format would still pass all ACs.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC2 marker verification command; Approach — aspect 1 description ('fanned into the finder passes (round_a/round_b)' and 'logical criterion id `project.<name>`')
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC2 markers list to: `['round_a','round_b','project.','logical criterion id','effective routing','criteria eval','configuration error']`
